content: Drospirenone has the potential to increase the plasma levels or pharmacological effects of various drugs by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of these interactions is generally considered minor or unknown. Below are the detailed interactions: 1. Fenofibrate: Drospirenone may elevate the levels or effects of fenofibrate by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. 2. Fenofibrate Micronized: Similarly, drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of micronized fenofibrate. 3. Fenofibric Acid: Drospirenone may enhance the levels or effects of fenofibric acid. 4. Fentanyl: Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of fentanyl. 5. Fentanyl Intranasal: Drospirenone may elevate the levels or effects of intranasal fentanyl. 6. Fentanyl Transdermal: Drospirenone may enhance the levels or effects of transdermal fentanyl. 7. Fentanyl Transmucosal: Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of transmucosal fentanyl. 8. Finerenone: Drospirenone may elevate the levels or effects of finerenone. 9. Flibanserin: Drospirenone may enhance the levels or effects of flibanserin. 10. Flutamide: Drospirenone may enhance the levels or effects of flutamide. 13. Fluticasone Furoate: Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of fluticasone furoate. 14. Fluticasone Inhaled: Drospirenone may elevate the levels or effects of inhaled fluticasone. 15. Forskolin: Forskolin may potentiate the effects of drospirenone through pharmacodynamic synergism. 16.
